claim: Cochin Port Authority's own history says it 'is believed' the port formed in AD 1341 from heavy Periyar floods that silted up Muziris and opened a new mouth at Cochin; it gives no study for this.

evidence.locator: History > Evolution of Cochin Port, para 1 (cochinport_timeline.txt / cochinport_evolution.txt)
evidence.quote: It is believed that the Cochin Port was formed in AD 1341 as a result of the heavy floods in the river Periyar.
The then harbour Muziris got silted up during the floods and a new opening formed at Cochin.
Cochin Saga by Sir Robert Bristow

note: Attribution claim only. The flood mechanism itself is NOT verified (see C006).

claim: 1341 is the start year of the Puthuvaippu ('new deposit') era used to date old Cochin deeds.

evidence.locator: Vol./page with Vypin island entry, OCR line ~24078
evidence.quote: dated in the Pucluvaippn (literally, new deposit) era, commen- cing A. I). 1341.
The second era the year Pooda Vaipum; which they call the new style
This was 383 years ago.

method: method/era_check.py: Visscher writes in 1723 that the era began 383 years earlier = 1340; Menon 1911 gives 1341 (1-year difference, counting convention unknown).
note: Logan, Malabar Manual (1887) also gives A.D. 1341 for the 'Putuveppu' era (examined, not cited: lite rule).

claim: The era marks the appearance of Vypin island from the sea, or perhaps only the first people settling it; the records themselves hedge which.

evidence.quote: The date of its appearance or, more probably, of the peopling of the place is preserved in old Cochin deeds
was first established when the island of

note: Visscher's full sentence: 'when the island of Vypeen was recovered from the sea and inhabited by men' (OCR stray marks between words). Say 'appeared or was settled', never 'was created by a flood'.

claim: Vypin is the island between the Cochin and Cranganur (Kodungallur) bar-mouths, formed of river silt; Menon says it formed only in the fourteenth century, its name meaning 'new deposit'.

evidence.locator: Physical features, backwaters para, OCR line ~1140-1141
evidence.quote: the island between the Cochin and Cranganur bars, called Vaipin or Pudu Vaiptt, was formed only in the fourteenth century.
The island has been formed by the deposit of silt brought down by the rivers discharging into the hack- water and the sea.

evidence.locator: footnote to backwaters para, OCR line ~1153
evidence.quote: and Pudu Vaipu, new deposit

claim: The 1911 State Manual says the name Cochin was first given to the town that grew up after the harbour formed in 1341, and that Pliny, Ptolemy, the Periplus, Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta do not mention Cochin.

evidence.quote: have been given first to the town which came into existence after the formation of the harbour in 1341
No mention of Cochin is therefore found in the earlier notices of Malabar.

note: Menon's survey, not ours: we did not open Pliny, Ptolemy, Periplus, Marco Polo or Ibn Battuta. Voice as 'a 1911 state history noted'.

claim: None of the pre-1912 records we hold (Visscher 1723, Logan 1887, Menon 1911) ties the 1341 era or Vypin to a flood, the Periyar or Muziris; the flood-and-Muziris mechanism appears only in the modern port page (hedged) and is described in a 2022 paper as an attribution.

evidence.quote: It is believed that the Cochin Port was formed in AD 1341
The date of its appearance or, more probably, of the peopling of the place
This was 383 years ago.

method: method/era_check.py searches 600 characters either side of every era/island passage in the three period texts for flood|inundat|deluge|Periyar|Alwaye river|Muziris; only hit is Menon's 'monsoon inundations are normal' (farm yields, not formation). Output: method/era_check_output.txt
note: Negative finding within our holdings only; peer-reviewed geomorphology (Padmalal et al. 2014, Quaternary International 325) was NOT opened (lite rule). Nunn & Kumar 2022 (examined, not cited) write that the 1341 change 'has been attributed to' a rainfall flood.

claim: The sand bar at the mouth of Cochin harbour was cut open on 30 March 1928, and the first vessel, SS Padma, crossed the channel into the harbour on 26 May 1928.

evidence.quote: Sand bar at the mouth of the harbour cut open.
SS Padma of
The first ship entered the Cochin harbour on 26th May 1928.

note: Port's own administrative record; strong for 20th-century dates.

claim: Harbour engineer Robert Bristow arrived on 13 April 1920 and, over about two decades (1920-1941), turned Cochin from an open roadstead into a modern harbour by cutting a shipping channel through the sand bar.

evidence.quote: Arrival of Sir Robert Bristow.
The transformation of Cochin from a mere roadstead into a modern harbour is credited to Sir Robert Bristow

claim: The port's timeline lists 1341 as 'Closure of the ancient port of Muziris and widening of Cochin Gut'.

evidence.quote: Closure of the ancient port of Muziris and widening of Cochin Gut.

note: Attribution only: no period source we read links Muziris to 1341.
